judgments.reason: The nonsensical phrase “for which it is not which is” is a mechanical drafting error affecting the operation of the settlement hammer.

neg128.clause_name: Endorsement 7.C. Basic Extended Reporting Period (90 Days)
neg128.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Invalid section reference in Extended Reporting Period Endorsement
judgments.reason: The endorsement's “Section VIL” reference fails to identify the actual Extended Reporting Period section, Section VIII.

judgments.title: Invalid section reference in Non-Owned Disposal Sites Endorsement
judgments.reason: The reference to “Section VL” mechanically misidentifies Section VI, Exclusions.

judgments.title: Invalid section reference in Transportation Coverage Endorsement
judgments.reason: “Section VL” is an invalid cross-reference where the intended Vehicles exclusion is in Section VI.

neg138.clause_name: Endorsement 11 — Schedule of Non-Owned Covered Locations
neg138.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Typo in "Bradfordt"
judgments.reason: “Bradfordt” appears to be a mechanical error in a scheduled street address and may affect identification of the covered location.

judgments.title: Odor Exclusion Added by CAFO Endorsement — Material for Poultry Operations
judgments.reason: The replacement definition expressly states that a pollution condition does not include odor; the resulting coverage gap is clear.

judgments.title: Invalid section reference in CAFO Endorsement
judgments.reason: The CAFO endorsement's “Section VL” reference mechanically misidentifies Section VI, Exclusions.

judgments.title: Products Pollution Sublimit — Per-Occurrence and Aggregate Both $1M
judgments.reason: Setting both the per-condition and aggregate products-pollution sublimits at $1 million clearly permits one event to exhaust the aggregate.

judgments.title: Duplicative "On or After" Language in Products Pollution Endorsement
judgments.reason: The duplicated words “on or after the” are an obvious redundancy and leave the intended temporal threshold unchanged.

judgments.title: Products Pollution Endorsement Includes "Remediation Costs" in Aggregate Despite Coverage Grant Excluding Them
judgments.reason: The products-pollution grant mentions claims and defense expense, while the related limits provision also lists remediation costs; reading the endorsement as a whole leaves uncertainty over whether that reference merely caps or implicitly contemplates remediation coverage.

judgments.title: Insured vs. Insured Exclusion — No Carve-Out for Subrogation or Contribution Claims
judgments.reason: The insured-versus-insured exclusion unambiguously bars claims between insureds without the proposed carve-outs.

judgments.title: Pre-Counsel-Selection Defense Costs Not Covered
judgments.reason: The exclusion of pre-selection defense costs and denial of SIR credit are explicit coverage choices, not ambiguities or internal conflicts.

judgments.title: Independent Counsel Fee Cap Disadvantageous to Insured
judgments.reason: The fee cap based on rates actually paid to comparable panel counsel is ascertainable, even if disadvantageous to the insured.

judgments.title: Typo in "inciuding"
judgments.reason: “Inciuding” is an obvious misspelling of “including” and does not alter the provision's meaning.

judgments.title: Environmental Consultant Pre-Approval Required Except for Emergency Response
judgments.reason: The prior-written-consent requirement and emergency exception are clear; the absence of a response deadline is a negotiation concern rather than a construction defect.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Limits of Liability
judgments.reason: Although not separately defined, “Limits of Liability” is repeatedly tied to the specific amounts in Items 2, 3, and 4 and is not genuinely ambiguous.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Limits of Liability
judgments.reason: The phrase is consistently linked to the specific limits in Declarations Items 2, 3, and 4, so no separate formal definition is needed to ascertain its meaning.

judgments.title: 100% Minimum Earned Premium
judgments.reason: The 100% minimum-earned premium is commercially harsh but textually clear; the cancellation refund provision can be harmonized because no premium remains unearned.

judgments.title: Typo in "Hlicit"
judgments.reason: Labeling the defined term “Hlicit abandonment” rather than “Illicit abandonment” creates a mechanical mismatch with the term used elsewhere in the policy.

judgments.title: Remediation Costs Require Environmental Law — Gap for Emerging Contaminants
judgments.reason: The phrase limiting remediation to that required by environmental law, together with the specific fungi and legionella exception, clearly excludes other voluntary remediation.

judgments.title: Typo in "exnenses"
judgments.reason: The quoted contract text reads “expenses,” and even the alleged spelling error would not alter the exclusion's meaning.

judgments.title: Fines and Penalties Exclusion — Multiplied Damages Carve-Out Missing
judgments.reason: The exclusion lists multiplied damages while the carve-back mentions only punitive and exemplary damages, clearly leaving multiplied damages excluded rather than creating uncertain list scope.

judgments.title: Fraud Exclusion Applied to "Responsible Person" During Policy Period — Broad Scope
judgments.reason: The fraud exclusion deliberately applies to any defined responsible person, and the Separation of Insureds clause expressly excepts that exclusion; the breadth is a coverage choice.

judgments.title: Internal Expenses Exclusion — Insurer "Sole Discretion" Standard
judgments.reason: The specific grant of approval authority at the Insurer's “sole discretion” conflicts with Section IX.M's operative requirement that insurer consent not be unreasonably withheld, delayed, conditioned, or denied.

neg65.clause_name: VI.M. Exclusion — Material Change in Risk
neg65.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Material Change in Risk Exclusion — No Notice and Cure Mechanism
judgments.reason: The lack of a notice-and-cure mechanism is an omitted favorable term, not an ambiguity or inconsistency in the exclusion as written.

judgments.title: Undefined term: covered operations
judgments.reason: The quoted phrase “covered operations” limits Coverage B but has no definition, creating genuine uncertainty about which operations qualify.

neg71.clause_name: VII.A. Notice of Claim or Pollution Condition
neg71.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Verbal Notice Requirement for Pollution Conditions — Vague Standard
judgments.reason: The term “immediate” in the verbal-notice requirement has an uncertain temporal boundary, particularly when coupled with the duty merely to take “all reasonable measures.”

judgments.title: Insurer Step-In Right with Costs Charged to Insured
judgments.reason: The “sole judgment” language clearly assigns the step-in determination to the Insurer; the absence of notice and cure is a negotiation issue.

neg75.clause_name: VIII.A. Entitlement to Extended Reporting Period
neg75.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Insurer's Mitigation Costs Subject to SIR and Limits — Reduces Insurer Recovery
judgments.reason: The provision clearly treats step-in remediation costs as insured-incurred costs subject to the SIR and limits; the absence of an additional reimbursement remedy is an omitted term.

judgments.title: Supplemental ERP Cost — Up to 200% of Premium
judgments.reason: “Not more than” 200% supplies only a ceiling and leaves the actual supplemental-ERP price within a broad range unstated, creating uncertainty over the purchase price.

judgments.title: No Express Prejudice Requirement for Late Notice
judgments.reason: The absence of an express prejudice rule or late-notice remedy is a legal-enforcement and negotiation issue, not an internal textual defect.

judgments.title: Non-Owned Covered Locations — No Separate SIR or Sublimit
judgments.reason: In the absence of a special SIR or sublimit, the policy's ordinary retention and limits apply; that result is clear despite the asserted underwriting concern.

judgments.title: Subrogation Recovery Waterfall Disadvantages the Insurer
judgments.reason: The recovery waterfall expressly states the order of payment; its priority for the insured is a clear economic term.

judgments.title: Application Statements Elevated to "Warranties"
judgments.reason: Calling application statements “warranties” is a clear substantive allocation of risk, notwithstanding its potentially severe legal effect.

judgments.title: Other Insurance Clause — Policy Always Excess
judgments.reason: The policy's excess position is clear; possible circularity arises only from provisions in separate insurance contracts, not from this instrument itself.

judgments.title: No Assignment Without Insurer Consent
judgments.reason: The anti-assignment provision clearly requires an endorsement, and the absence of corporate-transaction exceptions is a negotiation issue.

judgments.title: General Consent Clause May Undermine Insurer's Sole Discretion Rights
judgments.reason: Section IX.M's general prohibition against unreasonably withholding consent conflicts with the Internal Expenses provision granting approval authority at the Insurer's “sole discretion.”

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: insured
judgments.reason: The provision uses the policy's defined form, quoted lowercase “insured,” consistently; no capitalization defect or ambiguity is present.

judgments.title: Typo in "folowing"
judgments.reason: The matched text correctly says “following”; no meaning-changing drafting error is shown.

judgments.title: Additional Insured Coverage Limited to Vicarious Liability Only
judgments.reason: The endorsement expressly limits Hoffman Rettig's coverage to vicarious liability; any mismatch with a separate contractual obligation is external to this policy.

judgments.title: Incorrect subsection designation in Non-Owned Disposal Sites Endorsement
judgments.reason: Using “H.” between endorsement parts I and III is a mechanical numbering error; context indicates it should be Part II.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Sublimit of Liability
judgments.reason: The endorsement itself states the amount, its aggregate application, and its relationship to the policy limits, so the absence of a separate definition creates no material uncertainty.

judgments.title: Invalid section reference in Products Pollution Endorsement
judgments.reason: “EXLCUSIONS” is a harmless misspelling because the correct section number VI and the surrounding operative language unambiguously identify the intended section.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Sublimit of Liability
judgments.reason: Each endorsement specifies the relevant sublimit amount, what it caps, and that it is subject to overall limits, making the term operationally clear.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Deductible Period
judgments.reason: “Deductible Period” is assigned a duration of three days but is not defined, leaving some uncertainty about precisely how that waiting period is measured and applied.

judgments.title: Business Income Excludes Officer and Manager Payroll
judgments.reason: The parenthetical expressly excludes the listed payroll categories, creating a clear coverage limitation rather than a construction issue.

judgments.title: Business Income Definition May Allow Double-Counting
judgments.reason: Lost net profit plus continuing expenses is a conventional business-income formulation; net profit accounts for expenses in calculating profit, while the second component indemnifies expenses that continue to be paid.

pos1.clause_name: Section IX.I — Jurisdiction and Venue (forum-selection clause)
pos1.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: Fines and Penalties Exclusion — Punitive Damages Exception May Expand Coverage
judgments.reason: The phrase “insurable by law” does not itself identify the jurisdiction whose public-policy rules govern, even though the New York choice-of-law clause may ultimately resolve the question.

pos2.clause_name: Service of Suit Endorsement (No. 15) — submission to jurisdiction of any competent court
pos2.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: Service of Suit Endorsement Conflicts with Exclusive NY Jurisdiction
judgments.reason: The Service of Suit Endorsement permits submission to any court of competent jurisdiction, directly conflicting with Section IX.I's exclusive New York forum requirement.
